pages.text: When the lighthouse lit, it was bedtime. Mom waved a toothbrush and sang. "Brush, then sleep!" Dari hid under his quilt. "Too much trouble! I'll just sleep!" He covered his head.
Mom offered the brush, but Dari shook his head. "Can't I skip just once?" At last he fell asleep without brushing.
In the night, his teeth felt sticky and itchy. Bits of shell from dinner hid between them. Dari touched his cheek and woke. "Something feels funny..."
Mom hurried over with a little lamp. "Hidden shell crumbs are playing tricks. Let's sweep them out!" She held Dari's flipper.
As Mom told an imaginary story, Dari pictured shell crumbs rolling and giggling on white teeth. "Those pests were poking me!"
Mom whispered, "Crumbs fear white foam waves! Your brush is a wave broom, and toothpaste foam sweeps the rocks clean!" Dari lifted his front end out of the quilt.
Dari sprang up and went to the bathroom. Toothpaste on the brush! Up, down—bubbly waves! Shell crumbs rolled away in the foam. "Brush, brush, sparkle!"
Dari rinsed and opened wide. His teeth shone! The itch vanished as if washed away by waves. He slapped his tail. "I did it!"
Next morning, as the lighthouse light went off, Dari picked up his brush first. "One, brush when I wake! Two, brush before bed! Three, up and down, all over!" Kkiruk echoed the song outside.
Mom kissed his forehead. "Teeth shining like the lighthouse!" Daily brushing kept shell crumbs away. "Brush, brush, sparkle!" Dari smiled, showing all his teeth.
